rules.note: Four-year term. The election due in May 2026 was postponed: on 9 March 2026 Parliament extended its own mandate by two years because of the 2026 Lebanon war, so the next election is scheduled for May 2028 (Wikipedia: 2028 Lebanese general election). A decree of 2 February 2026 had set 1-10 May 2026.

The President is elected by Parliament: two thirds of the members in the first round, an absolute majority (65) in later rounds (Wikipedia: 2022-2025 Lebanese presidential election). The presidency was vacant for long periods after the 2007, 2014 and 2022 terms.

historical.note: All 128 seats. Seat counts for the four parties are those in the Wikipedia infobox; 'others' is the remainder (Progressive Socialist Party 8, Kataeb 4, Armenian Revolutionary Federation 3, Marada Movement 2, Independence Movement 2 per the infobox, with independents and other lists, including members of the Hezbollah, Amal, FPM and LF blocs who are not party members). The Future Movement did not take part: Saad Hariri announced on 24 January 2022 that he was suspending his role, and former Future politicians held 8 seats (Wikipedia). Hezbollah and its allies lost their parliamentary majority but the Speaker, Nabih Berri, was re-elected. Turnout 49.19%.

Parliament elected Joseph Aoun, the Commander of the Lebanese Armed Forces, on 9 January 2025 after the presidency had been vacant since 31 October 2022 and eleven earlier sessions in which no candidate was elected. First round: Aoun 71 votes (the 86 needed was not reached); the infobox gives 99 votes (77.34%) for Aoun and 2 for Chibli Mallat. Shares are of 128 members.
